title: Residency scenario mapping and contract implications
content:
Purpose
This working doc maps realistic customer residency requests (what they mean operationally) to enforcement options, telemetry needs, and downstream contract language we should offer sales/legal. Goal: create a short catalogue that PM/sales/legal can reference when negotiating commitments and engineers can use to implement consistent operator behavior and tests.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Customers use "territory-binding" requests with different guarantees: soft-binding (preference), hard-binding (data-at-rest location + processing location), and sovereign-only (private deployment with local KMS + audit evidence).
- Each guarantee has different operational costs and telemetry needs; we should map pricing tiers and sample contract clauses to make tradeoffs explicit.
- This doc contains: scenario matrix, acceptance checklist per scenario, simulation plan and cost-impact model, operator runbook sketch, and open questions for legal/finance.

Terminology used here
- territory-binding: customer-level preference or obligation that their tenant data must remain in a specific territory (country/region).
- local-processing: inference runs in compute physically located in the requested territory (including edge zones).
- anchor-storage: canonical storage copy anchored in the territory (can be multi-replica inside the territory).
- soft vs hard binding: soft = best-effort preference with documented fallbacks; hard = contractual obligation with penalties for violations.

Scenario matrix (customer asks -> operational interpretation)
1) Preference-only (soft)
   - asks: "Keep data in EU to the extent possible"
   - ops: route by affinity; prefer EU pools; fall back to nearest compatible pool with tag + audit reason
   - telemetry: percent routed to EU, fallback reasons, latency deltas
   - contract impact: note in SOC/standard terms; no SLA change
   - typical cost impact: low (routing inefficiency), negligible additional infra commits

2) Region-bound processing (hard)
   - asks: "All inference must run on compute inside FR/DE/UK"
   - ops: enforce model serving layer region constraint; reject requests that cannot be satisfied; provide audit logs
   - telemetry: per-request region assertion, evidence bundle (timestamped region tag + node id), error-rate for rejects
   - contract impact: SLA for availability in region; price uplift for reserved capacity; remedies for sustained inability to serve
   - cost impact: medium–high (dedicated capacity, reduced burst sharing)

3) Anchor + ephemeral external processing (hybrid)
   - asks: "Store canonical customer data in-country but allow transient inference elsewhere if transient copies are ephemeral and deleted"
   - ops: store anchor in region; route KV cache/compute to other zones but enforce ephemeral TTL + deletion proofs
   - telemetry: anchor store logs, ephemeral copy lifecycle events, deletion confirmations
   - contract: explicit TTL/deletion attachment + compliance audit clause
   - cost impact: medium (storage + network transfer + additional deletion proofs)

4) Fully sovereign (private deployment)
   - asks: "Private control plane in our VPC or on-premise; KMS in-country; no exfiltration allowed"
   - ops: customer-managed control plane; our package for runtime; optional remote support w/ strict access controls
   - telemetry: customer-provided audit logs; Redwood support-provided diagnostics minimal by contract
   - contract: license + support fees, change control, indemnities, exit clause for data extraction
   - cost impact: high (engineering support, distribution of packages, on-prem ops assistance)

Acceptance checklist (operator-oriented) for region-bound processing (hard)
- [ ] Tenant region declared and persisted in metadata registry
- [ ] Model versions available in target region catalog
- [ ] Route-liveness test: synthetic requests served with region assertion headers >= 99.9% for ten minutes
- [ ] Audit evidence generation: per-request bundle with node_id, zone_id, timestamp, hash of input
- [ ] Telemetry hooks: fallback counter, reject counter, region-violation alert
- [ ] Contract mapping: price uplift id assigned to tenant billing profile
- [ ] Onboarding runbook executed and confirmed by customer security team

Simulation plan: how we measure cost/availability impact
- Input variables: tenant qps, model size (GB), seq length distribution, region commit level (soft/hard), locality churn (fraction of requests from outside territory)
- Simulations to run (prototype harness in /sim/residency-sims):
  1) 10k qps small-model EU hard-binding with shared pool fallbacks disabled
  2) 1k qps large-model with anchor-storage in APAC + ephemeral processing globally
  3) Mixed workload: 100 tenants with mixed binds (20 hard EU, 10 sovereign APAC, 70 soft-global)
- Metrics captured: P95 latency, token-cost delta, rejected-request rate, extra cross-region egress GB and associated $
- Deliverable: csv summary + cost delta heatmap (per tenant type) + operator playbook recommendations

Billing and contract implications (templates / suggestions)
- Soft-binding: no price change; include best-effort note and telemetry reporting frequency (monthly)
- Hard-binding: fixed monthly reserved capacity fee + per-token on-demand escalator for burst beyond reserved pool; include objective evidence clause (audit bundle) and SLA credits if region unavailable beyond grace period
- Sovereign/private: setup fee + annual license + support tiers. KMS in-customer region incurs managed-key surcharge. Add change-control clause for software updates and access windows.
- Suggested contract language snippets (for legal):
  - "Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to ensure processing occurs within the declared territory. For Hard-Binding agreements, Redwood will provision and maintain dedicated capacity as described in Exhibit A. Failure to meet availability targets will result in SLA credits as specified in Exhibit B."

Operator runbook sketch for a hard-binding incident (region outage)
1) Pager: oncall-eng + private-deployments-eng
2) Validate: check telemetry for region-node heartbeats and service liveness
3) If region completely unreachable: mark tenant impacted; notify SOC and customer success with pre-approved templated message
4) Fallback policy only if contract allows: spin up temporary dedicated capacity in alternate region and log explicit customer acceptance; otherwise initiate remediation sprint with infra and exec escalation
5) Postmortem: include audit-evidence showing attempts to keep processing local, timeline of decisions, and cost of remediation

Open questions and negotiation tradeoffs (for PM/Legal)
- What is minimum evidence bundle we can reasonably provide without leaking infra topology? (legal wants node-level evidence; infra worries about exposing internal IDs)
- How aggressive should automatic fallback be for hard contracts? Allow manual override by customer at onboarding?
- Pricing models: flat reserved or committed burst credit? Finance to model a 2-tier offering for SMB vs enterprise.

Action items
- Engineering: prototype evidence bundle format (PR in platform repo) — owner: Samir — due 2025-02-02 (WIP)
- Product: convert billing options into sales SKU language and test with two existing trial customers — owner: Diego — due 2025-01-10
- Legal/Contracts: draft Exhibit A/B templates for hard-binding and sovereign agreements — owner: Priya — due 2025-01-24
- SRE: create synthetic test harness in sim cluster and run scenarios 1–3 — owner: Elena — due 2025-02-12

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: it tries to connect operator reality (what we can log, what we can enforce) with contract language and pricing. Expect iterations with Legal and Finance.
- I intentionally avoided using the internal term "pin" in customer-facing docs; prefer "territory-binding" or "region-bound processing".
- Pending: link to telemetry schema (TODO: add when platform PR merges).

Raw brainstorm snippets (keep here for context)
- Could we accept a "soft-hard hybrid" where contract requires region routing but allows automated 8-hour fallback window during sustained outage with different SLA? Might be acceptable to some customers if priced correctly.
- Consider supporting a lightweight cryptographic proof-of-location for nodes (signed region assertion) to satisfy auditors without exposing infra inventories.
- Investigate per-tenant geo-anchoring TTLs to reduce cost for tenants that only need occasional in-region retention.

End of doc
